# RecipeManifest

Namespace `Nfty.Core.Model` in assembly `Nfty.Ticket`.

```csharp
public record RecipeManifest : ISchemaVersioned
```

A complete template for one character type: which layers, in what order, and which combinations are illegal.

```csharp
public RecipeManifest(string Id, string Name, IReadOnlyList<string> LayerOrder, IReadOnlyList<IncompatibilityRule> Rules, int SchemaVersion = 2, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, double>? AbsentPercent = null, bool PartialAlpha = false);
```

**Parameters**

- `Id` (`string`) - Stable identifier, unique within its CookBook.
- `Name` (`string`) - Display name.
- `LayerOrder` (`IReadOnlyList<string>`) - Ingredient ids bottom-to-top. This — not the ingredient collection's own order — is what generation rolls and composites, so an ingredient missing from it is never drawn.
- `Rules` (`IReadOnlyList<IncompatibilityRule>`) - Incompatibility rules applied to a rolled selection; a violation costs a re-roll.
- `SchemaVersion` (`int`) - The manifest format version; see [`Schema`](Nfty.Core.Model.Schema.md).
- `AbsentPercent` (`IReadOnlyDictionary<string, double>?`) - How often each layer is left out entirely, as a PERCENT, keyed by ingredient id. A layer not named here always appears, which is why the whole dictionary is optional and null by default. **It lives on the Recipe, and it could not live anywhere else.** An `.igt` is a standalone file that a Kitchen hands to any project, so whether a Hat *appears* is not a property of the hat artwork — the same ingredient is guaranteed in one recipe and a chase item in another. This is the same shape [`CookBookManifest.RecipeWeights`](Nfty.Core.Model.CookBookManifest.md#p-recipeweights) already uses one level up: a dictionary on the parent, keyed by the child's id. **A percent, not a probability, and the unit is in the name.** 0..1 would mean a conversion at every boundary a human touches — the CLI option, the form field, the report — and each one is a chance to divide by a hundred twice or not at all. This converts exactly once, in the roller. **A chance, not an absent WEIGHT**, because a weight is unstable: store one and then double every variant weight, and the layer silently gets commoner without anyone touching it. A chance survives variant edits, which is what an author means by "15% of the time". 100 means the layer never appears — shelved without deleting, the same thing a recipe weight of 0 already means one level up. Added after schemaVersion 1 and therefore OPTIONAL with a null default, for the same reasons spelled out on [`CookBookManifest.TargetSupply`](Nfty.Core.Model.CookBookManifest.md#p-targetsupply): `Schema.Current` is deliberately NOT bumped.
- `PartialAlpha` (`bool`) - Whether any variant under this manifest carries a partial-alpha pixel — the book-level value is what the UI calls "2D only". A listing cache: writers stamp it from the pixels on every write, and anything that decoded the pixels recomputes it rather than reading it.

## Properties

### AbsentPercent { #p-absentpercent }

```csharp
public IReadOnlyDictionary<string, double>? AbsentPercent { get; init; }
```

How often each layer is left out entirely, as a PERCENT, keyed by ingredient id. A layer not named here always appears, which is why the whole dictionary is optional and null by default.

**It lives on the Recipe, and it could not live anywhere else.** An `.igt` is a standalone file that a Kitchen hands to any project, so whether a Hat *appears* is not a property of the hat artwork — the same ingredient is guaranteed in one recipe and a chase item in another. This is the same shape [`CookBookManifest.RecipeWeights`](Nfty.Core.Model.CookBookManifest.md#p-recipeweights) already uses one level up: a dictionary on the parent, keyed by the child's id.

**A percent, not a probability, and the unit is in the name.** 0..1 would mean a conversion at every boundary a human touches — the CLI option, the form field, the report — and each one is a chance to divide by a hundred twice or not at all. This converts exactly once, in the roller.

**A chance, not an absent WEIGHT**, because a weight is unstable: store one and then double every variant weight, and the layer silently gets commoner without anyone touching it. A chance survives variant edits, which is what an author means by "15% of the time".

100 means the layer never appears — shelved without deleting, the same thing a recipe weight of 0 already means one level up. Added after schemaVersion 1 and therefore OPTIONAL with a null default, for the same reasons spelled out on [`CookBookManifest.TargetSupply`](Nfty.Core.Model.CookBookManifest.md#p-targetsupply): `Schema.Current` is deliberately NOT bumped.

### HasOptionalLayers { #p-hasoptionallayers }

```csharp
public bool HasOptionalLayers { get; }
```

Whether any layer of this recipe can be left out. This is what the GUI's "optional layers" toggle reads: the toggle is DERIVED from the data rather than stored beside it, so the two can never disagree about whether the feature is on.

```csharp
public double AbsentPercentOf(string ingredientId);
```

How often one layer is left out, as a percent. Zero for a layer that always appears, which is every layer of a recipe that does not use the feature.

**Parameters**

**Returns.** 0..100.
